data.name: Ephrayim
data.gender_notes: Ephrayim is used as a male name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Two sons in the womb, Ephraim and Manasseh, whom Joseph adopted as his own sons. The name Ephrayim carries the meaning “Double fruit of the womb” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Ephrayim usually hope their child will grow to embody double fruit of the womb and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A symbol of God's blessings and adoption.
data.etymology: Ephrayim belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Double fruit of the womb.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Ephrayim total 5, giving a life-path number of 5. Number 5 is linked with Mercury and with the qualities of freedom, adaptability and curiosity.

in_english.name: Ephraim
in_english.long_meaning: From the Hebrew, meaning 'fruitful' or 'double fruitful' or 'two fish', and derived from the root 'aphar' which means 'to bear fruit'.

data.cultural_impact: Ephrayim reflects the cultural and spiritual values of the Biblical tradition and is used in Christian communities.
data.spiritual_significance: In Jewish tradition, the name Ephraim is believed to have deep spiritual significance as it symbolizes the idea of adoption. Joseph adopted Ephraim and Manasseh, and their namesake became synonymous with the idea of being taken in and accepted into a new family or community. In this vein, the name Ephraim can represent the idea of inclusion, acceptance, and the ability to start anew. Additionally, the name Ephraim is also connected to the name El-Phraim, which means "God the father of Phraim," further emphasizing the idea of God's love, protection, and nurturing care for the Israelites.
data.spiritual_symbolism: The name Ephrayim carries profound spiritual symbolism as it is rooted in Biblical tradition. The meaning "Double fruit of the womb" symbolizes Two sons in the womb, Ephraim and Manasseh, whom Joseph adopted as his own sons.. In Christian spirituality, bearing the name Ephrayim serves as a constant reminder of one's spiritual calling and connection to Christian values of double fruit of the womb.

biblical_reference.note: The second son of Joseph and Asenath, born in Egypt. Ephraim and his brother Manasseh were adopted by Jacob as his sons.

name_in_real_life.story: James Ephrayim from Jerusalem, Israel embodies the meaning of Ephrayim - "Double fruit of the womb". Raised in a Christian family, they were taught to honor the significance of their name and walk in faith throughout their life.
